terms.title: The work
terms.body: I review the MyAlly code, database rules and build spec and deliver what is listed in Exhibit A. That's all Step 1 includes. Steps 2 and 3, the build, a pilot and any launch each need their own written yes.

terms.title: Fee
terms.body: {{fee_step1}} fixed, for up to {{hours_step1}} hours of my time, paid before work starts. Extra work only with your written OK, at {{rate_ff}} an hour.

terms.title: Timing
terms.body: About {{duration_days|weeks}} after I have access. Delays on your side move the date by the same amount.

terms.title: Office hours
terms.body: {{oh_sessions|Word}} {{oh_slot_minutes}}-minute sessions a month ({{oh_free_hours}} hours) at no charge, while a step is active. Unused sessions don't roll over. Extra hours are {{rate_standard}} an hour, or {{rate_committed}} an hour when booked for {{commit_weeks}} weeks or more.

terms.title: What you own
terms.body: Once paid, you own the report and any code I write for you in Step 1. I keep my pre-existing tools, templates and methods, including ARCS, and you get a free, permanent license to use any of them that are part of what I deliver, for MyAlly.

terms.title: Estimates are mine
terms.body: Any ranges, estimates or plans are my good-faith planning numbers for work I would do. They are not a quote, a fixed price or a promise. You may use them inside MyAlly and with your investors, but not as a scope or spec for other vendors to bid against without my written OK.

terms.title: Opinion, not professional advice
terms.body: What I give you is my opinion, to use as you see fit. I am not your lawyer, accountant, compliance officer, security auditor or child-privacy expert. Nothing I provide is legal, regulatory, compliance (including FERPA, COPPA, HIPAA or state privacy law), medical, educational or certified security advice. Get qualified experts for those, and the decisions remain yours.

terms.title: As is
terms.body: The code, the report and everything else are provided as is, with no warranties of any kind, including that it is error-free, secure, compliant or fit for a purpose. Bugs, tech debt, maintenance, hosting, security, upkeep, backups and compliance remain your responsibility, unless a later written agreement says otherwise.

terms.title: Your data
terms.body: Please don't give me real family or child information. If the database holds real records, I review the rules, not the records.

terms.title: Limit of liability
terms.body: My total liability for anything under this agreement is capped at {{liability_cap}}. Neither of us is liable for indirect or lost-profit damages.

terms.title: Indemnity
terms.body: You will defend and cover me against claims from anyone else arising from your platform, your data, your users, or how you use my work. I will do the same for claims caused by my gross negligence or willful misconduct.

terms.title: Disputes
terms.body: We talk first, in good faith, for {{talk_first_days}} days. If that fails, binding arbitration in {{arbitration_venue}} under the American Arbitration Association's commercial rules, before one arbitrator. Small claims court stays open to either of us. Connecticut law applies.

terms.title: The NDA stays
terms.body: The Mutual NDA (executed {{nda_executed|nda}}) continues to apply, and this agreement counts as the services agreement in its section 8.1. If the two conflict on confidentiality, the NDA controls.

terms.title: Independent contractor
terms.body: I am not an employee. Either of us can end this agreement in writing, and you pay for work already done.

altitudes.strategic: Three cases (best, base, worst) and the guard for each. The worst case is Step 1 used as a spec for other bidders; terms 6 and 4 are the guard.
altitudes.operational: Three steps, each with its own written yes. Step 1 runs about {{duration_days|weeks}} from access.
altitudes.tactical: Chelsea's four asks, each answered by a named part of this record: deliverables, estimates, the delivery date and the agreement.
altitudes.surgical: Every value, where it came from, and when it last changed.

cold_read.why: My Ally said yes to Step 1 of a three-step offer. Before work starts, Chelsea asked four things, and their counsel will review the agreement.
cold_read.what: One record for this engagement. The reply email, the Step 1 agreement and its Exhibit A (deliverables) all render from it, so a changed price or date changes every page that cites it.
cold_read.why_now: The holding reply promised a follow-up. They want results before year end, and the NDA's return-or-destroy clause (8.1(c)) fires {{nda_return_by|long}} unless a services agreement is signed first.
cold_read.before: Agreement signed and GitHub and Lovable access by {{access_by|long}}.
cold_read.during: Step 1 runs about {{duration_days|weeks}}, {{hours_step1}} hours of my time, from {{access_by}} to {{deliver_by}}.
cold_read.after: A {{walkthrough_minutes}}-minute walkthrough by {{deliver_by|long}}, then their written yes or no on Step 2.

counsel_notes: Expect counsel to push back on the one-sided indemnity in term 11 (a mutual version is the usual compromise), the term 6 limit on sharing with other vendors, and arbitration replacing the NDA's choice of Connecticut courts. Hold firm on terms 7, 8 and 10.
